name: Anterior thalamic nuclei
summary: The anterior nuclear group forms the tubercle at the front of the thalamus and is a station on the Papez circuit of memory: it receives the mammillothalamic tract from the mammillary bodies (and direct fibers from the hippocampal formation via the fornix) and projects to the cingulate gyrus. Lesions of the nuclei or of the mammillothalamic tract, as in tuberothalamic and paramedian infarcts, produce amnesia, and the nucleus is a target for deep brain stimulation in epilepsy.

anatomy.location: Anterosuperior pole of the thalamus, bulging into the floor of the lateral ventricle behind the foramen of Monro, enclosed by the anterior limb of the internal medullary lamina.

efferents.via: anterior limb of the internal capsule

function: Relay of hippocampal–mammillary memory information to the cingulate cortex; contributes to spatial memory and to the propagation of seizures through the limbic circuit.

bestView.label: anterior thalamic tubercle behind the foramen of Monro
anterior pole of the thalamus below the fornix

imaging.normalAppearance: The anterior tubercle is identifiable on axial T1 as the anterior tip of the thalamus; individual nuclei are not resolved. The mammillothalamic tract is visible on 7 T and on the Neudorfer atlas mesh in this atlas.

pathology.finding: Anterior thalamic restriction from the polar artery (a PComm branch) with amnesia, apathy and language change on the left.
Mammillary body atrophy with medial thalamic signal change.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: DWI; coronal T1 for mammillary bodies

lesionEffects.mechanism: Interruption of the Papez circuit at the anterior nucleus or mammillothalamic tract
Anterior thalamic connections to the cingulate and frontal cortex

examination: Registration and delayed recall of three words; recognition versus recall
pearls: Amnesia after a thalamic stroke means the anterior or mediodorsal nuclei or the mammillothalamic tract
Thiamine deficiency and thalamic stroke share the same memory circuit; both produce Korsakoff-type amnesia
